note: These two thresholds are NOT measured and are NOT probabilities. They are the
rule-tier band mapping spec section 11.3 asks for in its last paragraph, so that
the decision procedure has one shape across both engines before a probabilistic
engine exists.
The mapping. The rule engine reports one of four ordered tiers, whose values are
tier_values above and are stated in classify/base.py. tau_high sits at the MEDIUM
tier value, so HIGH and MEDIUM both land in the confident band; tau_low sits at the
LOW tier value, so a context-only match lands in the low band and becomes a note;
NONE falls below both and the tool says nothing.
Why MEDIUM is confident rather than low. MEDIUM is what an identifier, a
placeholder, or an option list earns. A name attribute reading cardnumber and a
select offering twelve months are strong, checkable evidence about a control, and
they are the only evidence a hostile page leaves standing. Putting them in the low
band would mean the tool could never say anything above a note about exactly the
pages it exists for. LOW is context only, which is prose near the control rather
than anything on it, and that genuinely is a near miss worth a note and no more.
target_precision, dev_precision, dev_recall, corpus_manifest_sha and derived_on are
null because nothing has been measured. P4 fixes a precision target before looking,
commits it under experiments/predictions/, computes the thresholds on the dev split,
and fills these keys in. Until then a null is the honest value and a plausible
number would be a law 3 violation sitting in a file the runtime reads.
